evidence.title: 三类 形制, 山墙 红色 (S47 section 3)
evidence.summary: S47 sorts the shrines in three types by form and notes that on the album the gable walls of seven of them are painted red, against grey or white on other buildings: 瑞应宫, 太岁坛, the 杏花春馆 earth shrine, the 北远山村 and 涵虚朗鉴 dragon shrines, 广育宫 and 多宝阁. A colour rule usable for the models.

evidence.title: 杏花春馆 土地祠 (S47 section 2.2)
evidence.summary: The main earth-god shrine of the garden, south-west of 杏花春馆, one bay, facing east, called 春雨轩土地庙 in the file of 1858. Xianfeng granted its two deities titles in February 1858, added tablets and a stele, and set spring and autumn rites. Palace file gives the measures in Qing feet; the shrine still received offerings in 1861.

evidence.title: 1861 年 五处上供 (S47 section 4)
evidence.summary: In the fifth month of 1861 offerings were still made at five surviving places: the 春雨轩 earth-god shrine, 吕祖亭 at 双鹤斋, the 观音庵 at 课农轩, and 河神庙 and 惠济祠 of Qichun Yuan. It says only that these were standing and in use after the fire.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v2, editors' note on 杏花春馆
evidence.summary: First a vegetable plot, plaque of 1727. 春雨轩 was added in 1755; around it 涧壑余清, 得树亭, 杏花村, 土地庙, 镜水斋, 吟籁亭, the gate 渊镜/屏岩, 抑斋, 翠微堂, 绿云酣. The editors say 春雨轩 and others survived 1860, and were lost around 1900.
